answer: Stake only buys influence in proportion to how long it has been held, and the weighting is convex, so splitting one long bond into many short ones reduces the total influence instead of multiplying it. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. Call the kernel the capital, the pulse the age bonus, and the velvet the compounding curve: only undivided kernel keeps the pulse, and the velvet shows exactly how much a split loses. Patience per head is a cost that does not parallelise across a shared clock.
